subject: Initialization lag causing p95/p99 spikes on Hosted API - FinLytics production
messages:
From: Ava Thompson <ava@finlytics.com>

Cc: FinLytics Platform Ops <ops@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Significant p95/p99 latency spikes since 08:40 — impacting production

Neha / Laura,

We started seeing a sharp regression in p95 and p99 for the /generate endpoint in our production integration around 08:40 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 4.8% and a subset of requests are timing out at 30s. The backlog shows many requests in INITIALIZING state. This is hitting our end-of-day batch jobs and causing failed trade reconciliations.

Sample request IDs: 83a1f2a4, 83a1f2b9, 83a1f30c.

Attached are a few traces and logs we captured. Can you confirm whether this is related to autoscaling / instance spin-up? We urgently need an ETA for a mitigation or workaround (will accept routing to a dedicated pool or warm instances).

This is P1 for us — our ops team will be on standby.

Thanks,
Ava Thompson
Platform Reliability Lead
FinLytics

Subject: Re: Significant p95/p99 latency spikes since 08:40 — impacting production

Preliminary SRE findings (quick summary):
- Investigated the Grafana dashboards and request traces: spike correlates precisely with a flurry of NEW_INSTANCE_CREATED events in the us-west-2 hosted GPU pool between 08:38–08:46 PT.
- Observed that model container startup + kernel JIT/quantization warm steps are taking ~13–18s on average for these instances; combined with request queueing this surfaces as p95/p99 of ~6–12s higher than baseline and occasional 30s timeouts for unlucky requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden scaling event (burst of concurrent batches) caused many instances to be provisioned simultaneously; warm cache/VFS + GPU kernel setup contributes significant tail.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (options):
A) Increase min_pool_size for the affected hosted pool to 2 (from 0) to keep warm capacity — low-risk config change, immediate effect.
B) Route FinLytics traffic to a lower-burstiness path (reserved warm pool / dedicated routing) — requires AE sign-off and likely billing discussion.
C) Deploy a small kernel-cache preload that reduces first-request JIT by ~30% — needs canary and a 2–4 hour rollout.

I've opened INF-1129 to track root cause and the longer-term fix. I recommend A) as a fast temporary measure while we run the preload canary.

Logs/links: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/latency/hosted-api?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2
Attached a filtered trace set we've pulled (finlytics-sample-traces-20260803.zip).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Significant p95/p99 latency spikes since 08:40 — impacting production

Ava — apologies for the disruption. We understand the severity and appreciate the traces you sent. We're going to enact an immediate mitigation while SRE runs the canary patch:
- Increase the warm pool for your traffic in us-west-2 to reduce cold-start probability (temporary).
- Apply a short-term credit for impacted requests for today — we'll confirm amount after we have stabilized latency.

Can you confirm if you want Redwood to proceed with increasing the min_pool_size (option A from Rishi)? That can be done within the next 10–15 minutes and should reduce the p99 tail for the next few hours.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:12:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant p95/p99 latency spikes since 08:40 — impacting production

Action taken: increased min_pool_size for hosted GPU pool (us-west-2) from 0 -> 2 for FinLytics routing; performed rolling restart of the autoscaler placement agent to ensure new policy is effective.

Initial observations (30m after change):
- p95 reduced from ~2.8s above baseline to ~0.6s above baseline.
- p99 shows marked improvement (reduced tail events); error rate dropped back toward baseline (~0.5%).

I'll continue to monitor and kick off the kernel-cache preload canary (INF-1129) this afternoon. Attaching notes from the infra change.

Attachments: infra-minpool-change-notes.txt

—Jonas
